Per ISO 14890 Table 5 Note 2, where heat resistance is required, cover properties (incl. abrasion, if wanted) must be separately agreed between manufacturer and purchaser. Indus Super Thermo is classified under ISO 4195 Class 1/2/3, not ISO 14890 H/D/L, so abrasion remains Not Specified unless separately agreed.

Class temperature tiers (Cl. 4.2): Class 1 = resistant up to 100°C | Class 2 = resistant up to 125°C | Class 3 = resistant up to 150°C. ISO 4195 does not distinguish lump vs. fine material — temperature applies to the test/service condition generally, not material form (see Note to Cl. 4.1).
Not Specified separately — ISO 4195 does not distinguish lump vs. fine material temperature limits; the same class temperature (Cl. 4.2) applies regardless of material form.

Exposure to heat per Cl. 4.3.1: full-thickness belt sample, 400mm × 400mm, cut from centre of belt ≥100mm from edges, placed in air oven per ISO 188 for 7 days (168 h) at: Class 1 = 100°C | Class 2 = 125°C | Class 3 = 150°C. Sample cooled after exposure before testing.

Not Specified by either standard. ISO 4195 does not address adhesion at all (Cl.1). ISO 14890 Cl.8.1 ageing requirement (168h at 70C) applies only to cover TENSILE STRENGTH and ELONGATION AT BREAK - it does not include adhesion. ISO 14890 Cl.15 adhesion values (Tables 9/10) are unaged/as-supplied values only; no post-ageing adhesion change limit is defined.

ISO 4195 does not specify belt breaking strength (outside scope, Cl.1). Per ISO 14890 Table 8, minimum full thickness tensile strength is selected from the designated belt type series (N/mm = kN/m of belt width): 160, 200, 250, 315, 400, 500, 630, 800, 1000, 1250, 1600, 2000, 2500, 3150. The specific designated value is selected per the ordered belt type (Cl.4.1(e)) - not a single fixed minimum across all constructions.

Not Specified - ISO 14890 Table 8 and Cl.14 specify minimum tensile strength only in the LONGITUDINAL (warp/length) direction of the finished belting; no minimum weft (transverse) tensile strength is mandated by ISO 14890 or ISO 4195.
Not Specified by either standard - no required weft-to-warp strength ratio is defined in ISO 14890 or ISO 4195.

fields.section: Not Specified (distinct from Cl.13 - see notes)
fields.notes: Not Specified as a MINIMUM by either standard. Caution: do not confuse with ISO 14890 Cl.13, which sets a MAXIMUM elongation of 4% - but that 4% limit applies at the reference force (10% of nominal tensile strength, Cl.3.2), not at break. ISO 14890 does not specify elongation at break at all; ISO 4195 only covers cover-rubber elongation at break (Table 1), not full-thickness belt elongation at break.

ISO 4195 does not address this (outside scope, Cl.1). Per ISO 14890 Cl.13: elongation of the finished belting in the longitudinal direction AT THE REFERENCE FORCE (defined Cl.3.2 as one-tenth of nominal tensile strength x test piece width) shall be NOT GREATER THAN 4%. This is exactly the "Elongation @ 10% Ref. Load" parameter - Maximum = 4%.

Not Specified - ISO 14890 Cl.13 elongation requirement applies only to the longitudinal (warp) direction; no weft-direction elongation at break or reference-force value is specified by either standard.

Not Specified - neither ISO 14890 nor ISO 4195 directly specifies a minimum elastic modulus value for the belt; it can be derived from tensile strength/elongation test data but is not itself a standard-mandated parameter.

ISO 4195 does not address adhesion (outside scope, Cl.1). Per ISO 14890 Table 9 (applies to synthetic filament carcass - EP/NN/EE fabric qualifies): minimum adhesion between cover and carcass - mean value 3.2 N/mm (covers 0.8-1.5mm thick) or 3.5 N/mm (covers >1.5mm thick); lowest graphically recorded peak value 2.4 N/mm or 2.9 N/mm respectively. Highest recorded peak value should not exceed 20 N/mm in any test (splicing consideration).

ISO 4195 does not address adhesion (outside scope, Cl.1). Per ISO 14890 Table 9: minimum adhesion BETWEEN ADJACENT PLIES - mean value 4.5 N/mm; lowest graphically recorded peak value 3.9 N/mm. Highest recorded peak value should not exceed 20 N/mm in any test.
Same basis as top cover to ply (Table 9): mean 3.2 N/mm (0.8-1.5mm covers) / 3.5 N/mm (>1.5mm covers); lowest peak 2.4 N/mm / 2.9 N/mm respectively.

ISO 4195 does not address troughability (outside scope, Cl.1). Per ISO 14890 Table 11, minimum F/L ratio at 35deg angle of inclination = 0.14. NOTE: ISO 14890 Table 11 defines troughability purely as a function of side-roller angle of inclination - it does NOT differentiate by belt width. The ">=650mm" width qualifier in this field has no basis in ISO 14890; the 0.14 minimum at 35deg applies regardless of belt width.

Same basis: ISO 14890 Table 11 minimum F/L ratio at 35deg = 0.14, independent of belt width. No separate value exists for a ">=2200mm width" bracket in ISO 14890 - this width-based split is not a feature of this standard.
Not Specified — ISO 4195:2012 covers only heat resistance (hardness, elongation, tensile strength variation after heat ageing); this parameter is outside its scope (Cl. 1).

Not Specified — ISO 4195:2012 covers only heat resistance (hardness, elongation, tensile strength variation after heat ageing); this parameter is outside its scope (Cl. 1).

ISO 4195 specifies test PIECE preparation (Cl.4.3.2) but no lot/batch sampling plan. ISO 14890 Cl.17 states: "Sampling shall be conducted in accordance with ISO 282" (Conveyor belts - Sampling). Neither document reproduces the ISO 282 sampling plan itself (lot size, AQL, sample count) - that detail resides in ISO 282, which was not supplied for cross-check.

Standard conditioning: 24 h at (23±2)°C and (50±5)% RH — atmosphere B per ISO 18573 (Cl. 4.3.2.1, 4.3.2.2). Alternate for textile-carcass belts (by agreement, noted in test report): (20±2)°C, (65±5)% RH — atmosphere A. Tropical conditions special case (ISO 23529): (27±2)°C, (65±5)% RH — atmosphere C.
Not Specified — ISO 4195:2012 does not define retest or rejection criteria; it specifies test method and reporting (Cl. 5) only, not acceptance/rejection rules.

fields.grade_description: Severe Cut and Gouge Service — metallic ores (as mined), limestone (quarried), granite (quarried), quartz, blast furnace clinker, slag, crushed metallic ores, sandstone, stone chippings, coke (cold), broken glass, gravel
Severe Abrasion Service — conveyance of very abrasive materials (defined by experience in each case)
Moderate Service — rubble, sharp sand, superphosphate, bone, coal (surface), ashes, unslaked lime, cement, sand (smooth), clay, slaked lime, charcoal, grain, vegetables, fruit, flour, wood chips

[Informative] Highest performance cover — intended for severe abrasion and cut/gouge service (e.g. metallic ores, quarried stone, gravel, coke, slag, crushed ores, sandstone, stone chippings). Highest tensile strength (24 MPa) and elongation (450%) with lowest permitted abrasion loss (120 mm³). Grades H, D and L are in accordance with ISO 10247.

[Informative] General purpose cover — intermediate performance for moderate abrasion service (e.g. coal, sand, earth, soft stone). Mid-range tensile strength (18 MPa), elongation (400%) and abrasion loss (max 100 mm³). Grades H, D and L are in accordance with ISO 10247.

[Informative] General purpose cover — standard duty for light to moderate abrasion service (e.g. grain, vegetables, flour, coal, sand, cement, clay). Lowest tensile strength minimum (15 MPa), lowest elongation minimum (350%), highest permitted abrasion loss (200 mm³). Grades H, D and L are in accordance with ISO 10247.
General purpose conveyor belting for standard-duty industrial and mining applications. Intended for materials causing moderate abrasion. Lowest tensile strength requirement among the DIN grades.

General purpose conveyor belting for moderate to heavy duty applications. Higher tensile strength and elongation than Grade Z. Intended for moderately abrasive materials (coal, grain, sand, soft stone).

Abrasion resistant conveyor belting for severe abrasion service. Highest tensile strength requirement (25 MPa). Intended for highly abrasive materials such as metallic ores, quarried stone, coke, slag, gravel.

Severe cut-and-gouge service — hard metallic ores (as mined), quarried limestone, granite, quartz, blast-furnace slag/clinker, coke, broken glass, gravel, crushed metallic ores, sandstone, stone chippings. Requires highest abrasion and cut/gouge resistance.
General heavy-duty service — coal, crushed stone, gravel, sand, general mining and quarrying. Moderate to high abrasion resistance required.

General purpose conveyor belting for moderate duty and typical industrial/mining applications. Intended for materials causing moderate abrasion (e.g. coal, grain, sand, soft stone, earth). Highest tensile strength and elongation requirements among the general purpose grades.

Abrasion resistant conveyor belting for severe abrasion service. Intended for conveying highly abrasive materials (e.g. hard metallic ores, quarried stone, gravel, coke, slag). Mandatory abrasion test with test piece rotating per AS 1683.21.

General purpose conveyor belting for standard duty industrial and mining applications. Intended for conveying materials causing moderate abrasion. Lower tensile strength and elongation requirements than Grade M. Abrasion test is optional — specified by purchaser per Appendix B(l) of AS 1332 : 2000.
